overall_summary: Space and cosmic anomaly topics are the clear drivers of reach and engagement on the channel, with videos about extreme planetary conditions (burning ice, coal-dark planets, supersonic rubies) consistently outperforming psychology and basic animal trivia. Viewers are highly attracted to extreme, sensory-driven cosmic facts, whereas standard brain facts and common animal trivia fail to capture interest.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (971 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (536 views) are the top-performing videos.
winning_patterns.action: Focus heavily on bizarre exoplanets, cosmic weather, and extreme space phenomena. Use highly sensory hooks (smell, color, extreme heat/cold) to spark immediate curiosity.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views) and 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (262 views) show solid mid-tier performance.
winning_patterns.action: Frame historical, geographical, or biological facts as impossible timelines or physical paradoxes that challenge common sense.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (3-53 views across multiple uploads) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently underperform.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard textbook psychology facts. If covering mind/brain topics, frame them as high-stakes mysteries, survival scenarios, or dark psychological phenomena.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (183 views) and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) struggle to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Steer clear of widely known animal facts. Pivot to cinematic animal survival stories or highly unusual, lesser-known evolutionary adaptations.

next_video.concept: The egg-shaped planet being eaten alive by its own star (WASP-12b).
next_video.opening_direction: Show a hyper-realistic cinematic render of a pitch-black, egg-shaped planet being violently stretched as its atmosphere is sucked into a giant star.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet is being distorted by intense gravity and has less than 10 million years left before it is completely consumed and erased.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the highly successful exoplanet theme (similar to TrES-2b and the Planet of Burning Ice) by combining extreme cosmic conditions with a high-stakes, time-sensitive threat.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' space scenario, such as 'What If the Moon Was Only 100 Miles Away?', to see if speculative cosmic physics can match the high performance of exoplanet facts.
